findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are not filtered out when the search query is empty
findings.body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early when `!searchQuery.trim()` (lines 61-63) before applying the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` filter on line 67. As a result, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are still displayed in the span attributes list whenever the search input is empty, and are only hidden once the user types a non-empty search query.

findings.title: Zipping error_ids with nodestore get_multi().values() mismatches IDs and payloads
findings.body: In `fetch_error_details`, `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dictionary keyed by `node_id` whose iteration order is not guaranteed to match `node_ids` and, in backends such as `DjangoNodeStorage`, omits keys that were not found in the database. Iterating via `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs `error_ids` by position with `events.values()`, associating `event_id`s with the wrong event data whenever the backend returns rows out of order or omits missing nodes. Look up each event by its `node_id` (e.g. `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids)` with `data = events.get(node_id)`).

findings.title: Truthiness check on age and timestamp allows 0 when both fields are present
findings.body: `BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`. Because `0` is falsy in Python and `0` is a valid non-negative value for both `age` (0ms elapsed since report generation in the W3C Reporting API) and `timestamp`, a report containing `age: 0` alongside `timestamp` (or `timestamp: 0` alongside `age`) bypasses the mutual-exclusion check. Check `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` and `self.initial_data.get("timestamp") is not None` instead.
